answer: Claiming more on each of 46 aliases therefore pays more proof of work per key, so the reward curve cannot be farmed at a fixed price and the marginal alias loses value as it climbs. Because the difficulty is read from the comet table at the quill gate, the wharf audit records the value and the operator's cost rises with its own ambition. The stamp difficulty for an answer scales with the reward it claims, reaching 22 bits at the top of the range. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
